chunks: 3. Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi narrated from Ahmad ibn Abu 'Abd Allah al-Barqi, from 'Abd al-'Azim ibn 'Abd Allah al-Hasani, from 'Ali ibn Asbat, from Sulayman, the freed slave of Tirbal, from Hisham al-Jawaliqi, who said: I asked Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him)

about the words of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'Glory be to Allah,' what is meant by it? He (peace be upon him) said: 'His transcendence (deanthropomorphism).' The chapter on the meaning of 'Allah is the Greatest.'
ai.seo_question: What is the theological meaning of 'Subhan Allah' according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) defines 'Subhan Allah' as 'Tanzih,' emphasizing God's absolute transcendence and purity from any anthropomorphic limitations or imperfections. This concise definition anchors the Shia theological concept of divine simplicity and serves as a foundational explanation for the chapter on 'Allahu Akbar,' linking praise directly to the affirmation of God's supreme magnitude.
